blockingFindings.kind: Unclosed safety/equivalence proof obligation; not a reproduced counterexample
blockingFindings.finding: Projection calls expand(s,g,h,true,true) and returns before actual output_text/JSONB materialization. Thus it omits the default branch actual octet_length(output_text)<=sizes[root] and pg_column_size(output_value)<=native_sizes[root] confirmations. The native recurrence is leaf actual nativeBytes, otherwise16+sum(child native bound+16+explicit-object key bytes). Its sufficiency for m/l flattening has not been established from attached authentic PostgreSQL17 evidence.
blockingFindings.concreteRiskClass: Merge compact v-object children with many numeric values in one child and short string values in another, using disjoint interleaving sorted keys. Global object key/value ordering can interleave the children differently from each separately measured compact object; resulting Numeric alignment padding may occur at value boundaries rather than only child boundaries. Constant16 per incoming edge does not by inspection prove domination of this changed padding. Both children can have valid unique keys and allowed sizes, so duplicate checks do not settle the size implication.
blockingFindings.hypothesisBoundary: This report contains no PostgreSQL17 layout investigation, no constructed/executed graph, no measured byte counts, and no claim that this class actually violates the bound. It identifies the exact missing implication. A future authentic layout proof may close it or reveal that a bound change is needed.

staticSourceChecks.duplicateKeys: For v-object leaves, raw payload parser already requires JSON WITH UNIQUE KEYS, including nested compact objects. o keys are counted under binary C collation. m flattens key sets over each actual edge using jsonb_array_elements rather than deduplicated child reachability; repeated nonempty shared children therefore count duplicate keys. Every reachable object is checked, including objects reached under arrays. Shared valid subgraphs need one validation; incoming-edge multiplicity remains in m duplicate counts.
staticSourceChecks.rootAndContractProjection: Root object key set must exist and exclude llmUsage/_llmUsageRef/_authStateRef/_authStoreRevision. testKostenAuftrag.version and serviceContractHash are projected through compact values, explicit o fields and flattened m buckets. C-collated exact key comparisons and final #>> text preserve string/numeric text semantics such as5 versus5.0. m path reachability uses UNION, but prior edge-multiplicity key validation makes more than one nonempty occurrence of the selected key invalid; empty repeated maps cannot contribute a selected field.
staticSourceChecks.CASAtomicity: FOR UPDATE, expected revision/state/usage proof conflict return, immutable node insertion, transaction seals, usage ledger booking, root update and trigger path are outside the changed validation branch. Available current CAS/assert_graph/assert_data/guards are byte-equal to frozen original proposal functions. No reduction of original expected-state or usage acceptance guard was identified.
staticSourceChecks.NEWRendererInteraction: The NEW renderer changes the full output materialization implementation and retains its final UNIQUE KEYS, actual text length and actual native-size checks. The graph-projection branch returns before renderer output generation, but shares its complete bounds prefix. Accordingly new renderer compatibility is partly compositional; it does not by itself prove omitted final size confirmations redundant.
staticSourceChecks.textBoundReasoning: Leaf text size is measured from the actual normalized JSONB value. o/a recurrence includes container delimiters, child sizes, key quoted text and conservative separators; m/l removes child outer delimiters and adds separators only between nonempty children. NEW renderer uses the same child flatten/empty predicates and normalized leaf tokens. This supports text-size domination structurally, but no general native layout bound is certified here.
staticSourceChecks.resourceRiskNotBenefit: Projection still materializes all reachable bodies and arrays of object key sets. Shared subtrees and key-set aggregates may have their own work/memory cost. Avoiding one logical output value is not evidence of a reduced full-group memory peak.
